item.title: SCP idea (draft available)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Procedures, Description, and an Interview. Open to adding more, such as testing logs, or diary entries.

Elevator Pitch: A child discovers he can make living shadow puppets on walls with a light source and his hands. Unfortunately, he doesn't know how to completely control them. Ends with implications that the Foundation may use him as a weapon.

Central Narrative: A child is playing under a blanket fort with his parents. After his father shows him how to make shadow puppets with a flashlight and his hands, the child follows suit. The shadows he makes are living, and proceed to "devour" his parents. After not seeing the family leave their house for a while, police are called to the scene. After they enter, gunshots are heard, and then shadows dart around the house. A junior researcher who lives nearby calls in the situation and Foundation agents contain the child. The junior researcher is assigned to the SCP and tries to calm him down, though he knows what the Foundation might do to the child.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story of an innocent child doing normal things that becomes under the control of the cold and calculating Foundation.

Additional Notes: As mentioned, I already have a sandbox page with the first draft written. I had written the majority of this idea in a notebook, and then transferred the idea to my sandbox before I had found out about greenlighting. I apologize for going out of order.

item.title: Re: SCP idea: Retroactive weight gain supplement
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

you start to gain memories from before you were born of being something not human.

This part seems to appear out of the blue. Like, you have all these properties about weight loss and then you mention this. What does this have to do with the rest of the concept? I mean, you can add a depth meaning to the pills thing, but you need to have some kind of build-up, not just making it to appear spontaneously.

That said, I think some kind of twist like that would be interesting. The anomaly itself is pretty basic, and I think something like this would help a lot to improve it. What are these "new memories" about? What's the meaning of these memories? Maybe some kind of being wanted us to remember them? Maybe that being created the pills in order to attract us by using a common human desire? If you focus on this part, I think your article would be very interesting.

I haven't decided yet how much it affects other people's memories

I think other people's memories would be unaffected. Like, maybe they just don't want to hurt the subject's feelings? Maybe the subject's in denial about what others say? This is a common effect of real eating disorders, so it would make this concept to feel somewhat realistic.

or physical records like pictures.

Like I said, maybe they're just in denial of these records? Or maybe they see the records in a different manner?

I haven't decided yet what happens if you stop taking the pills, though it probably depends on if you have passed the critical point or not.

Maybe if they stop eating the pills, the memories slowly start to get back to normal? Maybe they forget about eating the pills in the first place? Maybe they start to have some kind of side effects? Perhaps the pills are like a drug?

Overall, I think that you should add some kind of backstory to the existence of the pills.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Class-D claims to be an 05
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): mainly mystery, slight comedy,

Page Layout (Optional): Aiming to make it as short and simple as I can

Elevator Pitch: A Class-D claims to be an 05-14, no proof of him being an 05, but there is mystery as how he got this way.

Central Narrative: There is a Class-D who claims to be an 05 council member. Due to little evidence supporting him, and a history supporting him being a Class-D, they do not make him an 05. However, they do not terminate him at the end of the month and make him a SCP because he knows stuff only an 05 knows.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: At the end of the SCP in an addendum, the site director says something like, "We do not know for certain that he is an 05 despite him having classified information. He could be an attempt at infiltration by a GoI, a Class-D who anomalously got his hands on classified information and is attempting to avoid end-of-the-month termination. Maybe he actually is 05-14 and was placed as a Class-D. We really do not know anything about him, and it is much safer to simply contain him than to blindly trust any assumptions. Rest assured, we are investigating this."

Additional Notes: If I manage to fit it in somehow, I can imply that some sort of group inside the Foundation intend to put him back up into the 05 council. As in, maybe some guard slips him a note saying that he believes him, and intends to break him out/investigate it himself. Also, apologies for any mistakes I make, this is my first post ever on the site and I really want to start writing an article after lurking for a couple of years.

item.title: Re: “Anti foundation” SCP
item.content:encoded:
You've got two basic problems:

1) What exactly is the goal of the "anti-foundations"? Are they trying to destroy The Foundation from within, steal SCPs, steal information, and/or slow it down? If they just worship the deity and only hate The Foundation, that's not in and of itself enough to create an MTF to take the people out. The most likely event is that they would tag the personnel involved and round them up, keeping them under control until they can figure out what's going on.

If they've all been marked MIA, it's likely that they would be found out during debriefing, something that The Foundation does a thorough job of considering that they deal with shapeshifters, possessors, and other infiltrators. Someone who was marked as MIA but came back would be seen as very suspicious under The Foundation's circumstances, and so the debriefing would be very thorough. As such, they would likely be caught by agents with no need for an MTF.

Unless, of course, they gained some sort of combat enhancement through their experience…

2) There either is an entity of some sort or there isn't. Since there is an effect, there has to be an entity of some sort. As such you need to actually define it. The fewer the mysteries the better, and if it's just a mystery for the sake of a mystery, that won't cut it.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Aquí Hubo Escena
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

he ends up risking up the veil and getting the community he so much loved killed

What happened? What did he do? I'm guessing it has something to do with the memetic agent. Did they all start to feel the 'bad' effects? Did he try to improve the feelings of his music? Also, why did he get persecuted? You're being very ambiguous with this part; I think you should explain this a little more in order to understand the exact things that happened.

he releases the memetic agent with ambiguous motivations.

Why did he release it? What was he thinking? Was he sad, angry, impulsive…? I don't see any motive to release the agent on a global scale. I think you should explain his motives in your concept post; even if they're going to be ambiguous in the article, you should have them clear in your mind.

is it really better to live on your knees than to die on your feet?

What? When did that dilemma come to be? Why is it a part of the story? It seems to appear out of the blue, and I don't see any connection with the story about a guy trying to improve his music. How are you going to portray this in your article?

Is the Foundation really willing to declare a war on artistic expression for the greater good?

What? What happened in order for the Foundation to declare open war on something? Did the agent get out of control? What happened to the world? You didn't say anything about this part in your concept.

Overall, I think your concept is missing some key points regarding the story you're planning to tell.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: Re: seeking greenlights: a forest clearing
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

The pocket dimension is something like a paradise version of the original forest clearing

I think you should explain a little more on this. What do you mean by 'paradise'? What's different from the real forest? You can play with the descriptions and/or physics of the pocket dimension. I think you should try to make the reader into 'feel' the sensation of what is like to be there.

in the middle of the forest clearing is an old ruin

Who lived there? Why no one lives there anymore? You can play with this. What was life like in there? You can have a lot of worldbuilding here. Maybe you can use it to show how a civilization living in "paradise" rose and fell? Maybe you can make this a metaphor of utopias and their inevitable collapse?

the portal got unstable and is now neutralized

This part could also be a metaphor about "dream places" being destined to collapse. This would be a nice and simple ending to a good story.

the will to stay in the pd grows with the time

Maybe, along with the pd, the traces of the civilization also grow? This way your story will have some type of escalation through the article. Maybe you could write one exploration log about a D-Class going in there and being happy while discovering the place's history?

if anyone tries to force someone to exit the pd after they spent more than 13 min in it, they'll do everything just to stay there

So how did the person who got lost even get out? I think they would've never leave, just because they would've not feel the necessity to do so. I think you should either get rid of this property, or came up with another story regarding its discovery. Maybe some disappearances? Maybe a group of friends find it and one of them got inside and didn't want to exit?

Overall, you have the opportunity to do a lot of worldbuilding here, and I think that would improve your article.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: Re: Greenlight time?
item.content:encoded:
1) The reviewers are major sticklers on the 400-word limit. Also, you're going to need to collapse it down using the following string: [G[collapsible]G] collapsed text [G[/collapsible]G] (just eliminate the Gs and put a lot of text in place of the "collapsed text" part (check the wiki text quick reference under the box for more information).

+ show block
– hide block

2) The big problem you have is that Coyote has already escaped into the metanarrative in the real world (he's featured in the White Wolf Werewolf: The Apocalypse as a major spirit as well as a number of webcomics and other media, such as the American Gods books and even Marvel Comics). It's hard to keep a good trickster contained.

3) Keep in mind also that as a trickster, and one that's been doing it for aeons, Coyote will find a loophole, assuming it's not a bluff to keep attention over here as he does something over there. Out of all of the various deities you could mess with, this is one of the trickier ones simply because Coyote is known for his schemes.

Ironically, that makes him a good pick for this, but there has to be a reason for him to behave other than his personal honor.

4) This would be better for Tales than as an article. Also, I'm sort of worried about the "tragic" tag; Coyote just doesn't do tragedy. He generally comes out on top and making fun of all of those involved, sometimes even himself. That The Foundation has handled gods is worth noting, especially in this case.

5) The Chaos Insurgency and Serpent's Hand are mutually antagonistic, both between themselves and The Foundation. While it appears that's allowed for with CI, it's unlikely that SH would help The Foundation. Also, as SH hates to contain entities, especially humanoid ones, I'm not sure that they would agree to do so themselves, especially one as potentially powerful as Coyote.

6) Overall, I think you may be trying to do too much with this, and you may want to break it down a little. You have a couple of different things going on, and any one of them (sapient stories, a character from myth, even a deity branching out) would be great to focus on. I'm just not sure one entry would do it justice.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Greenlight time?

item.title: A multidimensional book about records
item.content:encoded:
A book containing all the records set by any entity in any dimension in all of existence. (SCP version of Guinness world records but a multiversal edition)

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Drama/Emotional, Comedy,

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: The vehement struggle of a researcher coming to terms with the "record" his father holds.

Central Narrative: A researcher is tasked to read through the book containing countless records. Through fan post/mails send from all over the universes, he comes to learn that his idol, his father, is not the man he had imagined him to be. The book itself has no other anomalous qualities then depicting the records.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that the premise, of a record book in a world full of extremes, is an interesting idea and something which would draw a lot of attention, provided it is done in a sufficient manner. Many parallels to existing SCPs could be drawn as well. The conflict with the unspeakable atrocity the father might have committed should serve as the main point of interest.

-Whatever crime the father has committed will not be mentioned-

After a lengthy discussion on the critters forum, I came to the conclusion, that this idea is better suited for a tale. It is just a revisited idea of an older idea of mine here is a link to it http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13137282/scp-idea-a-multidimensional-book-about-records

And this is a modernized version of the first thread I had written about the tale idea. Back then, the idea was not fleshed out enough. link http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13675691/a-multidimensional-book-about-records#post-4759034

I do hope that it now is better suited for the said endeavour.

item.title: Re: Hydrophobic Fountain
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

While I like the core idea of a sentient fountain that produces hydrophia, I have a few concerns regarding it. The first one, and the most important, is about the way you're going to portray the fountain's consciousness. How are you going to do it? How does it communicate? Does it have a personality? Why did it decide to induce hydrophobia to the whole town?

My second concern is about the way you're going to structure the article. Are you going to do interviews, reports, journals, some kind of radio transmissions…? Are you planning to show the affected people's point of view?

This draft is about 2-3 years old.

While I think that the site's expectations have evolved, I've seen articles that old being still good ones, so I'm unsure whether this will affect the result or not.

Overall, and with the awareness that 'many reviewers liked it', I'm going to ask you to PM me a link to your draft. I would like to see how you developed this concept to make sure this is still up to the site expectations.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit.

17:47 <CurtisSnyder> I want to collaborate with people before I even consider starting a set story line
17:48 <CurtisSnyder> MalyceGraves: The SCP I'm writing deserves a Euclid tag however because it has killed someone who was being groomed to replace an 05 member, the 05 destroyed it. The EC is saying that this SCP shouldn't be neutralized at all as it can be easily contained, all you need are people with average IQ. So this is the starting of the conflict, eventually I
17:48 want the EC to start going behind the 05's back, maybe the next SCP they want neutralized is actually transported somewhere and is safe and sound, being contained by a mobile task force of some type. This will end with a 001 proposal with the 05 and the EC. Some type of agreement or some type of truth. I'm not sure what yet. (Sorry I had re-written
17:48 the conflict to make it seem more interesting)
17:51 <•MalyceGraves> CurtisSnyder: Ok, I want to narrow in on one aspect first. I'm not all that much of a fan of using IQ as an arbitrary dividing line between who is affected and who isn't by this thing. IQ itself is measurable by a wide variety of often inherently flawed metrics and isn't really that good at indicating who is "smart" and who isn't. Intellect itself is fluid and complex, so focusing on this could inevitably lead to your
17:51 having to define who is and is not considered "smart"
17:52 That can lead to complications that I'm not entirely certain you want.
17:53 <•MalyceGraves> IQ is fairly arbitrary in and of itself and appears to fluctuate a great deal across the spectrum of one's life. The idea of a weird SCP being the subject of conflict between the O5 Council and EC isn't a bad one, it's been done before
17:54 I've explored conflict between the two myself, actually
17:54 <CurtisSnyder> I'm down to change what the dividing line is, I'd like to make it interesting and hard to detect. I also want it to be (theoretically) able to kill an 05 member under the right circumstances. Did you have a suggestion on what that dividing line could be?
18:00 <CurtisSnyder> MalyceGraves: I'm down to change what the dividing line is, I'd like to make it interesting and hard to detect. I also want it to be (theoretically) able to kill an 05 member under the right circumstances. Did you have a suggestion on what that dividing line could be?
18:01 <•MalyceGraves> CurtisSnyder: Most of the various dividing lines would be fairly discriminatory in nature and could open various problems you probably dont want to explore. I suggest using something fairly simple. "People born on Tuesday" or "people between the ages of 17-28"
18:01 <CurtisSnyder> and by "an 05" I mean "all 05"
18:01 <•MalyceGraves> The story you're telling isn't about the anomaly, but about the conflict surrounding the item. You could lock it in a box and drop it into the ocean and no one would care about it
18:03 <CurtisSnyder> MalyceGraves: So you're saying that it doesn't have to be able to kill all of the 05 in order to be detrimental to The Foundation?
18:04 <•MalyceGraves> The story isn't the fact that this is dangerous. For whatever reason an o5 decides to destroy it, and the EC gets pissy about it
18:04 <•MalyceGraves> That's your story
18:05 <CurtisSnyder> Yeah, as I understand it, the EC is kind of a punching bag as The Foundation isn't known for it's proper ethics
18:05 <CurtisSnyder> However, they have power and can use it
18:11 <CurtisSnyder> MalyceGraves I appreciate the criticism by the way, I did have a question about the dividing line. Should their be some… explanation for why it effects the individuals it does?
18:12 <•MalyceGraves> CurtisSnyder: I wouldn't focus on that overmuch. Pick a reason, make it fairly low-threat and easy to block
18:12 <CurtisSnyder> MalyceGraves Do you think if I fleshed out the idea and got some more criticism, a greenlight would be possible?
18:14 <•MalyceGraves> Give me your link
18:14 Please
18:15 <CurtisSnyder> MalyceGraves: I haven't asked for a greenlight yet, however if you think I should then I will. http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13897865/seeking-criticism-before-seeking-greenlight-the-perfect-dish

I like the idea of the conflict between the O5s and EC. While that has been explored at some length elsewhere, it's still a concept that can be rehashed in interesting ways.

My takeaway from this conversation is this:

  • Anomalous item secured by the Foundation
  • Item is anomalous and dangerous, but easily secured
  • A high level Foundation Employee is killed by it
  • The O5s use their authority to neutralize the anomaly as a result
  • The EC gets upset by what they perceive as O5 over-reach for destroying something that could have been easily contained
  • Conflict ensues.

The specifics of what the anomaly is isn't what's important here. The conflict between the EC and the O5C is. The weird dishwasher with tongues is neat, I like that. Just don't use a dividing line that follows any of the usual tropes. As I said, picking something that has discriminatory baggage is probably a bad call. Use something arbitrary and innocuous like "born on Tuesday" or "Has an Aunt with a name that starts with the letter A". Something innocuous and boring is fine, because that's not the focus here.

Do that, and you'll be fine. Greenlight

item.title: Greenlight time?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mostly an exploration of a cool idea

Page Layout: Bog-standard SCP format

Elevator Pitch: The set of Indigenous American stories about Coyote are an anomalous set of living narrative and metanarrative characteristics, which the Foundation worries might "jump" into other contemporary narratives. "Coyote" fools the Foundation, involves the Chaos Insurgency, and eventually the Foundation hands the matter over to the Serpent's Hand, which seems to get the matter under control.

Central Narrative: There is definitely a plot to this, but I hope you'll find it interesting enough to warrant such a big explanation:

+ show block
– hide block

A culture's practices and beliefs determine its stories, right? But what if the stories start to have a mind (or agenda) of their own? A Foundation anthropologist reports that the set of stories about Coyote acts differently from any other set of stories about a character (indigenous or otherwise); specifically, the stories and the overall set itself shares Coyote's characteristics, as well as some some instinct for self preservation and an unknown degree of sapience.

The anthropologist, after being granted follow-up research funding, determines that "Coyote" has survived the general Native American genocide, and is still alive and kicking (and messing with anthropologists trying to pin him down). This worries the Foundation, who are concerned about what would happen if Coyote discovers how to (or maybe just decides to) jump into other contemporary narrative-sets. They have no idea what will happen in that scenario.

The Foundation does have a little trouble with the Ethics Committee; any sort of effective containment would be incredibly difficult, and would undoubtedly have numerous negative side-effects for the health of Native American cultures. The anthropologist suggests attempting to communicate with "Coyote" before initiating containment, which the Ethics Committee approves.

The anthropologist conducts a number of interviews with a wide selection of indigenous storytellers (and a few other unaffiliated anthropologists), and of course gets a diverse and slightly contradictory set of answers to the question "What would Coyote want in exchange for staying in a specific territory" (along with a few other questions). The anthropologist "concludes" that Coyote would want more funding and economic input going towards Native American affairs, healthcare, etc. Basically, he'd want the territory he's supposed to stay in bigger and "full of game".

A year later, Foundation web-sweeper bots detect a set of movie concepts, novel plots, and fanfiction arcs, many involving birds of some kind, which overall "behaved like a narrative animal, but with more personality", similarly to the Coyote set. The foundation at first classifies this as a new, similar SCP, but the anthropologist later realizes that it is in fact a containment breach, where "Coyote took the form of a bird". The site is taken down, and it is discovered that many of the original posts were made by the teenage daughter of a former member of the Chaos Insurgency of Kootenai descent.

An overseer note reveals that the anthropologist's superiors had suspected that he had other motivations for making the Foundation provide support to various reservations, due to him being Native American himself, but were willing to overlook that aspect so long as the containment worked. They interrogated the anthropologist to see if he purposefully leaked information to the Insurgency, or even blabbed to a friend, but he continually denies that he did, and says it's simply likely that "Coyote dumped us for the Insurgency". The overseer agrees, but the fact that Coyote was able to make himself discovered, instead of being discovered by the foundation, and the fact that Coyote double-crossed them (or made the Foundation think they had an agreement, when they were really only dealing with the anthropologist), means that he will be much harder to contain that originally thought.

A second overseer note records that a Foundation metaphysical entity containment expert suggested that they Foundation pass the issue on to the Serpent's Hand, provided they agree to the Foundation's terms and goal of containment. The movement was passed, and the Serpent's Hand eagerly agreed once contacted. The Foundation has been allowed a monthly "update" on containment, but the overseers are very aware that the SH could be lying to them and they wouldn't be able to tell. For now, they have kept the anthropologist and transferred him to monitoring overarching trends in pop culture, contemporary folklore, and internet culture for signs of Coyote. Otherwise, they hope the SH are doing an adequate job containing the SCP, which so far they appear to be.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation deals with a metanarrative SCP and gets hoodwinked. The Chaos Insurgency and the Serpent's Hand get involved (in ways which hopefully align with their modus operadii)

Additional Notes: The most important thing I want to watch out for is that I don't mis-portray parts of any Native American culture(s). That being said, this very much isn't the mythical figure of Coyote as an SCP (that'd be both stupid and impossible to write), but is a conscious set of stories which act similar to the character they portray. Whether it's an eventually explainable "strange pattern", or actually the mythical figure "hiding" in his own narrative, the point is to look at how the foundation will handle an SCP like this (of course there are others like it, but I hope this one proves an interesting expansion of the concept).

item.title: Re: Dionysus Asylum
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

First, the thing that I consider "bad":

is often used by the foundation to contain entities that aren't mentally stable.

How did they come to that decision? How did they discover it? I think it would be a huge security risk to put various anomalies in the same place, even more if they are mentally unstable. Also, what does the asylum's staff thinks about having people with superpowers as their patients?

excerpts from a journal written by a foundation MTF agent

Why is this journal important towards the anomaly? Why would the Foundation put this journal in the anomaly's documentation? Here, I think some interviews with the agent would be better, as the Foundation would see their improvement directly and immediately from week to week.

who was held captive by the Asylum

What? I thought the asylum was being used by the Foundation to help their own agents. How did the agent got inside the asylum? Did they were sent there, or they got inside by accident? I think it would be better to say that the Foundation send them to see how the asylum would work with people with PTSD.

encounters with other patients, most of which happen to have anomalous properties.

Were those patients in there before the Foundation found the asylum? I think it would be a huge security risk to send an MTF member into a place with various anomalies. I think you should specify the exact way the asylum works in order to keep its patients safe from each other.

the agent begins to comply with the treatment and is soon released

What's this treatment? Why is it different from the Foundation's treatment? You should specify the exact way the asylum works.

I also considered the asylum being immune to reality warping

While this would make sense in the context that the asylum is there to help anomalous entities, I feel like this would be a little like a Deus Ex Machina to contain overpowered entities. I think you should find another way to keep the place safe without giving it too much properties.

Now, the things that I consider "good":

Generally, I like the idea of twisting the "abandoned asylum" cliché into an actual psychiatric hopital, and I also like the idea of the Foundation using it to help its own anomalous humanoids. I think you have a chance of exploring the way an anomalous person interacts with other anomalous entities, and how they need a different treatment for mental issues. I think you should expand more on this idea.

the Asylum really does just want to help people.

I like anomalies that want to help people, and I think that this would work as some kind of twist at the middle of the article. Like, all of those strange creatures inside an abandoned asylum and then it turns out its just a normal psychiatric hospital.

Other things:

I think given the nature of this SCP and how the foundation uses it it'd probably be a Thaumiel but I'm not entirely sure.

I think it depend on the focus of the article, but it also seems like a Thaumiel to me.

Overall, you will have to do a great character development for this concept to succeed.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: Hikikomori
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Tabs for different security levels, each with different Special Containment Procedures. Clickable subsections within.

Elevator Pitch: A hikikomori ends up as a SCP entity by means of apparent suicide, becoming capable of entering reality from other people's dreams. Except that by doing so, he just discovered something very wrong about our reality.

Central Narrative: The ability to enter reality turns out to not be just a gimmick. Like the plot twist in the film "The Others", the roles are flipped: the SCP entity is more real that our waking life. Turns out that the SCP Foundation is protecting the waking reality itself by keeping that very secret. One of the things to do is to prevent real human contact with the hikikomori.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story uses a similar layered security format as SCP-2718. Accurate information about the SCP and the very existence of that information turns out to be what is being contained, besides the entity itself.

Additional Notes: I already have a complete draft ready. The article links to SCP-2718 and SCP-2000, which are significant inspirations. However, this is a more traditional SCP article that doesn't in any way attempt to copy those two, and lacks the sort of semirealistic narrative as used in SCP-2817. I did not want to link this to the Oneiroi lore, and generally there are very few links to other SCPs.

Elevator Pitch: An SCP that is friendly and compliant with containment, and will change its looks and actions to suit the observer best (it is an empathetic metamorph). There is a catch, though - any creature that has been in contact with it for an extended period of time will develop worrying symptoms that inclde an evental suicide, and these subjects are capable of indirectly spreading this "disease" (SCP-XXXX-2).
Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a friendly anomaly, found by the foundation after recieving reports of unnatural high suicide rates in North-West London. It was compliant with containment and is happy to stay isolated to guarantee the safety of others, thogh it is often reported to seem lonely and openly express this. However, it willingly stays in containment as to not endanger any more lives. It has often stated that it thinks SCP-XXXX-2 is the problem, and that it is simply infected with it, but research cannot be made of the matter.

item.title: SCP-XXXX
item.content:encoded:
Hello there. So I had this idea of a bedroom. It doesn't look abnormal at first glance. However, when one walk inside, they will enter a state of euphoria, giggling for no apparent reasons. When they do this, they are designated as SCP-XXX-A. Once in that euphoric state, they will grab as many pillows as they can find in the room, and exit it. They will then run around, looking for a human being. Then, once they found one, they will throw a pillow at the person and start a pillow fight with them. The "target" will be designated as SCP-XXX-B. If SCP-XXX-B catches the pillow, they will enter the same state of euphoria and fight back with the pillow. Once the fight is done, SCP-XXX-A will go back to looking for another human being to "contaminate", and SCP-XXX-B will do the same.

However, if the target doesn't catch the pillow, they will not enter the euphoric state, and SCP-XXX-A will be discontent, trying to throw it back at SCP-XXX-B until they catch it. If someone stays with SCP-XXX-A in the same room for around 10 minutes, they will enter the state of euphoria, even if they didn't catch the pillow, and the room they were in takes the same abnormal properties as the original SCP-XXXX.

Once contaminated, SCP-XXX-A will never leave that euphoric state and must be terminated.

Keter or Euclide class. I was thinking of calling it "The Best Slumber Party Ever".

What do you think ? Has something similar already been done ?

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Doctor Merigold! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey. We're very happy to see more people interested in extending their artistic skills with some knowledge you might only find here, on the SCP WIki. I can totally understand why you got attracted to the SCP Universe through its mysteries and secret knowledge sprinkled throughout its numerous articles - hopefully, you'll have as much fun reading them as the community had putting them together!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!
